newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures close lower, weak price action.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures close lower, weak price action.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed lower, and further declines are expected after June T-bonds failed to mount much of a corrective rally in the afternoon, traders said.
After the results of the five-year note auction were released, both June T-bonds and September Eurodollars trimmed losses, but only briefly.
"This whole pop up was used to re-set short positions," one bond futures floor trader said. "Just like Tuesday."
And like Tuesday, Wednesday's brief lift disintegrated and resulted in lower lows for the day.
"I had no idea we'd set a new low after that move higher," one bond futures trader said about June bonds' subsequent decline to 108-04/32.
"But it was disappointing that we didn't see a rise above 108-20/32," he said.

June T-bonds trimmed losses to 108-20/32 after the sale produced a yield of 6.66 percent, slightly below expectations. September Eurodollars, which had been trading heavy for most of the day, firmed fractionally above 93.75.
However, the sale's results turned into a distant memory under the shadow of the Fed's move to raise rates on Tuesday.

"In light of the fundamentals and signs that the economy is growing, I'd find it hard to believe that anybody is particularly enticed at this point," John Nyhoff, chief economist at Tokyo-Mitsubishi Futures (USA) Inc, said.
Nyhoff was referring to the U.S. February durable goods orders data, which knocked June bonds and most Eurodollars through key support levels on Wednesday morning.
Overall goods orders and orders ex-defense each rose 1.5 percent, much higher than average trade estimates.
The report suggested the Federal Reserve would raise rates at least one more time before the year was over, traders said.
"We generally don't even pay attention to the durable goods report," one trader said. "That just shows you how short the market is and that everyone is just looking for bad news."
Some Eurodollar traders felt that the Fed's move on Tuesday signalled the beginning of a rate cycle that would result in at least three more rate hikes.
"If we keep seeing strong data that will tell us the Fed will raise rates more than three times before the cycle is over," one Eurodollar trader said.
On Thursday, weekly U.S. jobless claims will be released at 0830 EST/1330 GMT. Claims are seen rising to 313,000, from 312,000 in the prior week.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were off 08/32 at 108-15/32, 10-year notes were 05/32 lower at 106-07/32, September Eurodollars were off 0.02 at 93.76 and December Eurodollars were off 0.035 at 93.51. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
